description:
Costs 5¢ per call. Checks your operating conditions against the part's absolute maximum ratings and recommended operating conditions; returns PASS / WARNING / FAIL / INSUFFICIENT_DATA per condition and overall.
Conditions by part type: converters and LDOs take input_voltage, output_voltage, output_current, ambient_temp, efficiency; MOSFETs take supply_voltage (VDS), output_current (ID), ambient_temp, power_dissipation; logic ICs take supply_voltage (VCC).
Verdicts:
- PASS: inside the recommended range, or at or below the derated limit. By default input_voltage and supply_voltage must stay at or below 80% of the absolute-maximum rating when no recommended maximum is known (inside a recommended range is a PASS), and output_current at or below 80% of its tightest rating; derating_pct changes this. Zero headroom on a rated current always warns. This is a screening policy; derating_reference cites the reliability guidance and its limits. Each check reports margin_pct against the raw limit, derating_pct and derated_limit.
- WARNING: within the limit but above the derated limit, above the recommended maximum but below the absolute maximum, or within 10% of an absolute maximum that isn't derated.
- FAIL: outside the range or over the limit.
- INSUFFICIENT_DATA: not safely checkable, usually an ambient_temp that could not be turned into a junction-temperature check. It never counts as a PASS.
Each check has limit_type (max / min / range / fixed); checks read from the datasheet text (source='llm') carry source_quote, the row the limit came from. A condition with no limit is listed in unmatched and holds the overall verdict at WARNING. If the ratings came from a different MPN than you asked for, resolved_as and data_quality_warning lead the response.
Temperature: ambient_temp is never silently compared with a junction limit. When the part's own dissipation is known, the tool estimates Tj = Ta + Pd × RθJA (RθJA from the datasheet's thermal table) and judges Tj against the junction limits, reported as 'temperature (junction est.)'. Pd by part type: LDO (Vin - Vout) × Iout; switching converter Vout × Iout × (1/η - 1), which needs efficiency; anything else, pass power_dissipation (for a MOSFET, ID² × RDS(on)). Without these the check is INSUFFICIENT_DATA and its note says what to pass. Current ratings are read at ambient_temp (a MOSFET's 25 °C drain current is derated towards its maximum junction temperature). temperature_basis says which basis was used.
Stored parameters answer instantly; anything else is read from the datasheet's ratings tables (validation_method says which). A part not yet extracted starts extraction and returns status='extracting' (not charged). A new datasheet takes about 2.5 minutes at the median and 6.5 minutes at the 90th percentile; a cold GPU start can take about 12 minutes. These are estimates, not deadlines.
Not for: transient or full thermal analysis (the junction estimate is a steady-state screen), MOSFET SOA curves (analyze_image the SOA graph), passives with no ratings table.
Example: check_design_fit('TPS54302', input_voltage=24, output_voltage=5, output_current=2.5, ambient_temp=70, efficiency=0.92)

derating_pct.description: Percent below a rating a PASS must stay, for input_voltage, supply_voltage and output_current. Default 20 (run at no more than 80% of the rating). 0 turns optional derating off; no current headroom still warns.

efficiency.description: Converter efficiency at this operating point, as a fraction (0.92) or a percentage (92). Lets the tool estimate a switching converter's junction temperature.

output_current.description: Output current / IOUT (A). For MOSFETs, this is drain current ID.

part_number.description: Specific manufacturer part number (MPN) or LCSC number (e.g. 'TPS54302DDCR', 'C2837938'). Not a value ('100nF'), description or reference designator ('R1').

power_dissipation.description: The part's own power dissipation (W), if you have worked it out (e.g. ID² × RDS(on) for a MOSFET). Used for the junction-temperature estimate.

supply_voltage.description: Supply voltage / VCC / VDD (V). For MOSFETs, VDS; compared against VDS(max) only.
